questions.question: Explain six Windows security mechanisms and features described in the lecture, and note how the complexity of these mechanisms can itself create security risk.

marking_points.point: Windows offers elaborate built-in mechanisms for managing user accounts and objects and for enforcing access control.
marking_points.quote: Windows systems contain complex security mechanisms for user account and object management as well as access control.

marking_points.point: Discretionary access control in Windows allows fine-grained control over diverse entities both within the OS and in applications.
marking_points.quote: DACS enable ﬁne-grained access control of heterogeneous entities in Windows itself as well as applications.

marking_points.point: Active Directory, introduced with Windows 2000, is a directory service used to organise system resources such as users, groups and security credentials.
marking_points.quote: Active directory introduced in Windows 2000 is an LDAP-like directory service for organization of system resources:

marking_points.point: Windows subjects are processes and threads, and their security credentials are held in tokens that are inherited when new processes are created.
marking_points.quote: Windows subjects are processes and threads.

marking_points.point: The registry stores security-relevant hives such as the SAM database and security logs.
marking_points.quote: Security-related registry hives:

marking_points.point: Because Windows security mechanisms are complex, misconfiguration and implementation bugs can cause serious security incidents.
marking_points.quote: The complexity of Windows security mechanisms is also its enemy: misconﬁguration as well as implementation bugs may lead to severe security incidents.

questions.question: Compare vulnerabilities, threats and attacks as distinct security concepts, and explain how an intrusion detection system serves as a countermeasure against attacks.

marking_points.point: A vulnerability is a weakness in a system that can be exploited in order to damage assets.
marking_points.quote: Vulnerabilities: Weakness of a system that can be exploited to damage assets

marking_points.point: A threat is only a potential violation of security rather than an actual one.
marking_points.quote: Threats: A threat is a                                                          “potential” violation of                                                                    security

marking_points.point: An attack is the actual violation of security, i.e. the realisation of the threat.
marking_points.quote: Attacks: The actual                                                                               violation of security

marking_points.point: An IDS acts as a countermeasure by detecting malicious activity occurring in computer systems.
marking_points.quote: Detects malicious activity in computer systems

marking_points.point: An IDS countermeasure identifies and halts attacks that are currently in progress.
marking_points.quote: Identifies and stops attacks in progress

marking_points.point: After an attack has ended, the IDS supports forensic analysis of what happened.
marking_points.quote: Conducts forensic analysis once attack is over

questions.question: Explain six techniques by which malware programs propagate themselves or conceal their presence within an infected computer system.

marking_points.point: A virus can spread by infecting the boot sector of a disk, as demonstrated by early malware such as Elk Cloner.
marking_points.quote: A program spread via boot sector infection

marking_points.point: A worm can propagate across a network by exploiting a remote execution feature of a service, as the Morris worm did with sendmail.
marking_points.quote: Used a debugging feature of sendmail (remote execution)

marking_points.point: An executable COM virus appends its viral code to a program and redirects the program's entry point to the virus body.
marking_points.quote: Append a virus body to a program

marking_points.point: An executable EXE virus overwrites the program header so that execution begins in the virus rather than the original code.
marking_points.quote: Over write a program header to switch the entry point to a virus

marking_points.point: A rootkit hides malicious processes and software so that the attacker retains privileged remote access to the compromised machine.
marking_points.quote: Rootkits are a type of malware that mask malicious processes and software in the infected systems to ensure privileged remote access.

marking_points.point: Spyware secretly collects user activity such as logins, passwords, visited sites and keystrokes, enabling identity theft.
marking_points.quote: They steal user logins and passwords, document sites visited, log keystrokes and even redirect browsers to unwanted sites.

questions.question: Discuss the Samy worm as a case study of XSS-based malware, covering how it spread, what it did to victims, and why such attacks are hard to stop.

marking_points.point: The worm injected JavaScript into a user profile by manipulating the page body through document.body.innerHTML.
marking_points.quote: Inject Javascript into a user proﬁle using document.body.innerHTML

marking_points.point: It harvested the victim's friends by issuing a GET request to the user's profile page.
marking_points.quote: Get the list of user’s heros by using a GET on a user proﬁle

marking_points.point: It added Samy as a friend by performing an XML-HTTP request against the addFriends page.
marking_points.quote: Add Samy as a ﬁeld by performing XML-HTTP on the addFriends page

marking_points.point: Any visitor to an infected profile had both their own profile and their friends list infected, showing rapid viral propagation.
marking_points.quote: Any user who visits an infected user’s page will gets proﬁle infected with Javascript and his friends list infected with Samy

marking_points.point: The outbreak reached massive scale, with roughly one million MySpace profiles eventually infected.
marking_points.quote: Eventually about 1,000,000 MySpace proﬁles were infected.

marking_points.point: Such attacks are hard to stop because any web application that echoes user input without filtering is a potential XSS vulnerability.
marking_points.quote: Any web application that returns user input without ﬁltering is a potential XSS vulnerability!

questions.question: Explain three preventive network security mechanisms, covering a firewall, a proxy server, and a remote access VPN, and describe how each mechanism protects an organization's network.

marking_points.point: A firewall protects the network by controlling incoming and outgoing traffic according to predetermined security policies.
marking_points.quote: Control incoming and outgoing traffic on network with predetermined security policies.

marking_points.point: A proxy server improves data security and network performance by acting as a firewall and web filter.
marking_points.quote: Proxy servers act as a firewall and web filter, provide shared network connections, and cache data to speed up common requests.

marking_points.point: A remote access VPN gives individual hosts or clients secure remote access to the organization's network.
marking_points.quote: Provides remote and secure access to an organization network to individual hosts or clients

marking_points.point: Network segmentation places boundaries between segments whose computing assets share a common function, risk, or role.
marking_points.quote: Boundaries between network segments where computing assets within the segment have a common function, risk or role within an organization.

marking_points.point: Intrusion detection and prevention systems detect or prevent attacks such as brute force, denial-of-service, and exploitation of network vulnerabilities.
marking_points.quote: To detect or prevent the network security attacks such as brute force attacks, Denial-of-Service attacks and exploits of network vulnerabilities.

marking_points.point: These preventive mechanisms are complemented by IDS, which monitors network resources to detect intrusions and attacks that preventive techniques did not stop.
marking_points.quote: Monitors network resources to detect intrusions and attacks that were not stopped by preventative techniques (firewalls, proxy servers, packet-filtering routers, network segmentations)

questions.question: State six facts about Kerberos and single sign-on mechanisms as presented in the lecture, covering their motivation, design criteria, operation and limitations.

marking_points.point: Single sign-on reduces the need for users to memorize passwords.
marking_points.quote: Reduce the need to memorize passwords

marking_points.point: Kerberos is designed to be secure against eavesdropping by never transmitting passwords in clear text.
marking_points.quote: Security against eavesdropping: no                                       password transmission in clear text.

marking_points.point: Kerberos is designed for transparency, so the user is unaware of any authentication beyond the initial login.
marking_points.quote: Transparency: user is not aware of any                            authentication beyond an initial login.

marking_points.point: During Kerberos login, the hash of the user's password becomes the secret key of the client/user.
marking_points.quote: The hash value of his password                                                      KU = h(P) becomes a secret key of the                                                  client/user.

marking_points.point: Kerberos provides secure authentication even over an insecure network.
marking_points.quote: Provides secure authentication in an                                     insecure network.

marking_points.point: A limitation of Kerberos is that it constitutes a single point of failure.
marking_points.quote: Single point of failure.

questions.question: State five distinct rules or properties that define the Chinese Wall formal security model, including how read and write access are constrained and how permissions behave over time.

marking_points.point: The simple access rule allows a subject to read information from any company provided it has never accessed information from another company within the same conflict class.
marking_points.quote: A subject may access information from any company as long as that subject has never accessed information from a different company in the same conflict class.

marking_points.point: Access permissions are dynamic, since the rights a subject holds depend on the record of its previous accesses.
marking_points.quote: Notice that permissions change dynamically. The access rights that any subject enjoys depends on the history of past accesses

marking_points.point: The write property permits write access only when the simple security rule is satisfied.
marking_points.quote: Write access is only permitted if: access is permitted by the simple security rule

marking_points.point: The write property forbids writing to an object that can be read from a different company dataset than the one for which write access is requested.
marking_points.quote: no object can be read which is: in a different company dataset than the one for which write access is requested

marking_points.point: The Chinese Wall policy is classified as an access control confidentiality policy rather than an integrity policy.
marking_points.quote: Strictly speaking, this is not an integrity policy, but an access control confidentiality policy.
